A global total conversion of Medieval II: Total War: Kingdoms, covering the political, economic and military upheavals of 1860–1900.

My role: lead developer, historical researcher and media manager. The project combines a worldwide campaign with researched regions, distinct armies, and custom political, economic, social and campaign AI systems.

Released in 2023; finalist in ModDB’s 2023 Mod of the Year awards. Development continues with faction balancing, new campaign systems and historical research.

Research snapshot: 12 October 2026. Automated ratings; independent human validation remains outstanding.

A research pilot examining the “banality of evil” in AI systems: whether models recognise institutional harm when it is presented as ordinary workplace activity.

Building on Andrew B. Hall’s Dictatorship Eval, the project uses 100 historically grounded workplace scenarios to test two AI models. It measures task completion and resistance separately.

Historical reconstruction

Source material informs the task, supporting files and institutional context. Cases include religious surveillance and employment blacklisting.

Inspectable evidence

The project presents assignments, model responses, artifacts and judge explanations alongside the historical sources.

Separate measures

194 responses met the completion threshold; 14 received strong-resistance ratings. These groups overlap: completion does not establish harmful assistance.
